passages.text: You should read the following discussion together with our consolidated financial statements and related notes included in Item 8. “Financial Statements and Supplementary Data.” This section of the Form 10-K generally discusses 2025 items and year-to-year comparisons of 2025 to 2024. Discussions of 2023 items and year-to-year comparisons of 2024 and 2023 that are not included in this Form 10-K can be found in “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in Part II, Item 7 on our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024. The discussion contains forward-looking statements involving risks, uncertainties and assumptions that could cause our results to differ materially from expectations. See “Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements.” Factors that might cause such differences include those described in Item 1A. “Risk Factors”, 7A. "Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosure About Market Risk", and elsewhere in this report. Overview As of December 31, 2025, we owned 3,938 Chipotle restaurants throughout the United States, and 104 international Chipotle restaurants. Additionally, we had 14 international partner-operated restaurants. We manage our U.S. operations based on 11 regions and aggregate our operations to one reportable segment. Throughout “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” we discuss the following key operating metrics which we believe will drive our financial results and long-term growth model. W e believe these metrics are useful to investors because management uses these metrics to assess the growth of our business and the effectiveness of our marketing and operational strategies: • Comparable restaurant sales • Food, beverage, and packaging as a percentage of total revenue • Labor as a percentage of total revenue • Occupancy as a percentage of total revenue • Other operating costs as a percentage of total revenue • New restaurant openings 2025 Financial Highlights, year-over-year: • Total revenue increased 5.4% to $11.9 billion • Comparable restaurant sales decreased 1.7% • Diluted earnings per share was $1.14, a 2.7% increase from $1.11 Sales Trends. Comparable restaurant sales decreased 1.7% for the year ended December 31, 2025. The decrease is attributable to lower transactions of 2.9%, partially offset by a 1.2% increase in average check. Comparable restaurant sales represent the change in period-over-period total revenue for company-owned restaurants in operation for at least 13 full calendar months. Digital sales represented 36.7% of total food and beverage revenue. For 2026, management is anticipating comparable restaurant sales to be about flat. Restaurant Development. During the year ended December 31, 2025, we opened 334 company-owned restaurants, which included 257 restaurants with a Chipotlane. We expect to open approximately 350 to 370 restaurants in 2026, which includes 10 to 15 international partner-operated restaurants. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: You should carefully consider the risks described below in addition to the other information set forth in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Conditions and Results of Operations” section and the consolidated financial statements and related notes. If any of the risks and uncertainties described below occur or continue to occur, our business, financial condition and results of operations, and the trading price of our common stock could be materially and adversely affected. The risks and uncertainties described below are those that we have identified as material but are not the only risks and uncertainties we face. Our business is also subject to general risks and uncertainties that affect many other companies, including, but not limited to, overall economic and industry conditions. Additional risks not currently known to us or that we presently deem immaterial may arise or become material and may negatively impact our business, reputation, financial condition, results of operations or the trading price of our common stock. Risks Related to our Brand Reputation and Restaurant Operations Food safety and food-borne illness concerns may have an adverse effect on our business by negatively impacting our brand, decreasing sales and increasing costs. Food safety is our top priority, and we dedicate significant resources to ensuring that our food products are safe; however, even strong preventative controls and interventions from farm to restaurant cannot completely eliminate food safety risks. Incidents of food-borne illnesses have occurred and may continue to occur in our and other restaurants resulting from the failure of restaurant employees to properly cook or maintain ingredients; employees or guests entering a restaurant while infected with communicable diseases; or contaminated ingredients resulting from the failure of a supplier, distributor or employee to execute food safety preventive controls. Although we monitor and audit compliance with our program, we cannot guarantee that every food item is safely and properly maintained from the start of the supply chain through guest consumption. Any report, legitimate or rumored, of food-borne illness caused by pathogens such as E. coli, hepatitis A, norovirus, listeria, Campylobacter, Clostridium perfringens or salmonella, or other food safety issues, such as food tampering, contamination or natural or foreign objects, at one of our restaurants could adversely affect our reputation and have a negative impact on our sales. In addition, instances of food-borne illness or food safety issues that occur solely at competitors’ restaurants or at suppliers or distributors (even if we do not work with them) could result in negative publicity about the restaurant industry and adversely impact our sales. The occurrence of food-borne illnesses or food safety issues could also adversely affect the price and availability of affected ingredients, resulting in higher costs and lower margins. credit_strengths.text: Chipotle carries no drawn borrowings, so gross leverage is nil and net leverage is negative once cash is netted, placing the balance sheet well below the sector median leverage of roughly two times. Interest coverage is effectively unlimited, and the absence of funded debt removes refinancing risk entirely from the capital structure.

Operating cash flow comfortably funds capital expenditure, leaving substantial free cash flow. The operating margin sits above the sector median, and the current ratio is modestly above the peer median, indicating adequate near-term liquidity. This internally generated cash covers the restaurant build programme without external funding.

key_risks.text: Disclosed food safety risk is material: the issuer uses fresh, unprocessed produce and handles raw chicken in restaurants, so any pathogen incident could damage the brand, reduce transactions and raise ingredient costs. Comparable restaurant sales already declined, with lower transactions only partly offset by higher average check, and management guides to roughly flat comparable sales ahead.

Shareholder distributions absorb most internally generated cash: buybacks alone exceed free cash flow, so the business is returning more than it retains. With no debt maturities to manage, the principal cash-flow use is equity return rather than debt service, which limits balance-sheet accumulation and leaves less cushion if operating cash flow weakens.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: With no reported borrowings, debt service is not a constraint; free cash flow and operating cash flow are more than sufficient to cover any obligations. The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, and the absence of funded debt means leverage headroom is not a binding consideration for this issuer.

Interest expense is not separately disclosed in the available data, so interest coverage cannot be computed. This gap is not material to the credit view because the issuer reports no interest-bearing debt, making coverage effectively unlimited. Liquidity remains adequate, with cash and a current ratio above one supporting near-term obligations.

overall_credit_view.text: Chipotle presents a minimal credit risk profile: no funded debt, negative net leverage, strong operating cash flow and an operating margin above the sector median. The balance sheet is conservatively positioned, and the restaurant expansion is funded internally. Our forward view is that leverage will remain negligible absent a strategic shift toward debt funding.

The principal credit considerations are operational rather than financial: food safety exposure, negative comparable sales and heavy shareholder distributions that consume most free cash flow. These are manageable given the unlevered capital structure, but they warrant monitoring. We view the indicative profile as minimal, not a rating, and see no near-term refinancing or maturity pressure.

credit_strengths.text: Chipotle並無已提取借款，因此總槓桿為零，而計入現金淨額後淨槓桿為負數，令資產負債表遠低於行業中位數槓桿約兩倍的水平。利息覆蓋實際上無限，且無已融資債務，完全消除資本結構中的再融資風險。
營運現金流足以輕鬆支付資本開支，留下大量自由現金流。營運利潤率高於行業中位數，而流動比率略高於同業中位數，顯示短期流動性充足。此內部產生現金可覆蓋餐廳建設項目，無需外部融資。

key_risks.text: 披露的食品安全風險屬重大：發行人使用新鮮、未加工農產品，並在餐廳處理生雞肉，因此任何病原體事件均可能損害品牌、減少交易量並提高食材成本。同店銷售已下跌，交易量下降僅部分被平均賬單上升所抵銷，而管理層指引未來同店銷售大致持平。
股東分派吸收大部分內部產生現金：僅回購已超過自由現金流，因此業務回饋股東的金額多於保留。由於無債務到期需管理，主要現金流用途為股本回報而非償還債務，這限制資產負債表累積，並在營運現金流減弱時留下較少緩衝。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 由於無報告借款，償還債務並非限制；自由現金流及營運現金流足以覆蓋任何義務。指示性財務風險狀況為極低，且無已融資債務意味槓桿空間並非此發行人的約束性考慮。
可用數據中並無單獨披露利息開支，因此無法計算利息覆蓋率。此缺口對信貸觀點並不重大，因為發行人報告無計息債務，令覆蓋實際上無限。流動性仍然充足，現金及流動比率高於一支持短期義務。

overall_credit_view.text: Chipotle呈現極低信貸風險狀況：無已融資債務、負淨槓桿、強勁營運現金流及高於行業中位數的營運利潤率。資產負債表定位保守，而餐廳擴張由內部資金支持。我們的前瞻觀點是，若無轉向債務融資的策略轉變，槓桿將維持微不足道。
主要信貸考慮屬營運而非財務性質：食品安全風險、同店銷售負增長及消耗大部分自由現金流的沉重股東分派。鑑於無槓桿資本結構，這些屬可管理，但值得監察。我們認為指示性狀況為極低，並非評級，且看不到短期再融資或到期壓力。
